title: Nesbitt–Shapiro inequality at the remaining endpoint values
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be the number of positive definite matrices in the cyclic sum, and let $F_p$ denote the corresponding cyclic expression. 

**Nesbitt–Shapiro endpoint conjecture.** If $p=12$ or $p=23$, then

$$
F_p\geq \frac{p}{2}n.
$$

The paper explains that this would, together with the preceding proposition and the known cases, establish the inequality for all remaining values in the stated ranges. The parser provides no evidence that these two cases have been resolved, so their status is open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.10933

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).
source_name: Projesh Nath Choudhury and K. C. Sivakumar, “Nesbitt and Shapiro Cyclic Sum Inequalities for Positive Definite Matrices”, arXiv:2110.10933 (2021).
